title_en: Poesis philosophica (Greek and Latin), [Geneva]: Henri Estienne, 1573: first page of the fragments of Heraclitus
title_el: Ποίησις φιλόσοφος (ελληνικά και λατινικά), [Γενεύη]: Ερρίκος Στέφανος, 1573: πρώτη σελίδα των αποσπασμάτων του Ηρακλείτου
licence: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (Internet Archive item record)
note: The page headed 'ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΗΡΑΚΛΕΙΤΟΥ ΤΟΥ ΕΦΕΣΙΟΥ / HERACLITI EPHESII QUAEDAM. Ex Sexto philosopho'. The scan is only 1531 px wide, so the full page is the download. Imprint from the Internet Archive record ('excudebat Henr. Stephanus', 1573); the place, Geneva, is not printed and comes from the Folger Library catalogue ('[Geneva] : Excudebat Henr. Stephanus, anno MDLXXIII'). Heraclitus' and Parmenides' words survive only as quotations in later authors, so there is no editio princeps in the usual sense: this anthology is the first printed collection of them (Commons calls it the 'first published anthology with presocratic texts'). The scan is a Google digitisation of a copy in the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale di Roma (ex-libris 'Ex Bibliotheca majori Coll. Rom. Societ. Jesu'). The page was identified from the Internet Archive's OCR text, not by looking at the image. The same book's title page is leaf 6 of this scan (archive.org/details/bub_gb_3J54VxKz_XUC/page/n6), and Commons has a separate photo of it from a Bloomsbury Auctions sale (File:Estienne_1573,_Poesis_philosophica.jpg, PD-US).

title_el: Ιάμβλιχος, Περί του Πυθαγορικού βίου (ελληνικά και λατινικά), επιμ. Λούντολφ Κύστερ, Άμστερνταμ: χήρα του Σεμπάστιαν Πέτσολντ, 1707: πρώτη σελίδα του Βίου του Πυθαγόρα
printer: Widow of Sebastian Petzold and her son Christian Petzold
licence: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (Internet Archive item record)
note: Chosen at the client's wish (6 November 2026) over the first edition, whose scan looked bleached white: a later edition on warm paper. Seen by eye on the downloaded file: 'Pag. 1' printed top right, the heading 'ΙΑΜΒΛΙΧΟΥ ΧΑΛΚΙΔΕΩΣ περὶ τοῦ ΠΥΘΑΓΟΡΙΚΟΥ ΒΙΟΥ ΛΟΓΟΣ, ΚΕΦ. α' beside 'JAMBLICHI CHALCIDENSIS DE VITA PYTHAGORAE LIBER UNUS, Cap. I', decorated initials E and C, Greek and Latin columns over Küster's notes. No headpiece. Warm tan paper, much like the approved Estienne 1573 scans. Greek text with Obrecht's Latin, edited by Küster; the volume adds Porphyry's Life of Pythagoras with Holstenius' and Rittershausen's notes. Imprint from the Internet Archive record ('Amstelodami : Apud Viduam Sebastiani Petzoldi'); catalogues add 'et filium ejus Christianum Petzoldum'. Not the first printing: Iamblichus' Life was first printed by Arcerius (Franeker, 1598), and I found no free colour scan of that. The thumb_url returns 1630 x 2246 (474 KB); the local file is that image scaled to 1200 px wide. Worth a second look: this is a private upload to the Internet Archive (2021, 600 ppi). The uploader set the Public Domain Mark but does not name the library or the source of the scan; the book itself is from 1707. A thin dark strip of the gutter shows at the left edge. The page is Iamblichus' Life only, not the Golden Verses. Alternatives in the same item: the title page in red and black with the Greek title (page n0, its left edge slightly cropped by the scan) and the engraved frontispiece of Pythagoras (page n1). Fallback with an institutional licence: the Wellcome Collection's colour photograph of Hierocles' commentary on the Golden Verses (ed. Curterius, Paris: Nicolas Nivelle, 1583), Public Domain Mark on its Internet Archive record; its Greek first page, with a headpiece and the heading ΙΕΡΟΚΛΕΟΥΣ ΦΙΛΟΣΟΦΟΥ ΕΙΣ ΤΑ ΠΥΘΑΓΟΡΕΙΩΝ ΕΠΗ ΥΠΟΜΝΗΜΑ, is https://archive.org/details/b3335179x/page/n35/mode/1up, but the small book is photographed on a dark background and would need cropping. title_en: Poesis philosophica (Greek and Latin), [Geneva]: Henri Estienne, 1573: first page of Parmenides' verses
title_el: Ποίησις φιλόσοφος (ελληνικά και λατινικά), [Γενεύη]: Ερρίκος Στέφανος, 1573: πρώτη σελίδα των στίχων του Παρμενίδη
licence: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (Internet Archive item record)
note: The page headed 'PARMENIDIS CARMINA. Ex Sexto philosopho' (p. 41 in the book's index). The scan is only 1623 px wide, so the full page is the download. Note: this is Parmenides' poem, as in library.json; if Plato's dialogue Parmenides was meant, Commons has its 1513 first page too (File:Parmenides_beginning._Editio_princeps.jpg, 1076 x 1908, 1.2 MB, PD-Art). Imprint from the Internet Archive record ('excudebat Henr. Stephanus', 1573); the place, Geneva, is not printed and comes from the Folger Library catalogue ('[Geneva] : Excudebat Henr. Stephanus, anno MDLXXIII'). Heraclitus' and Parmenides' words survive only as quotations in later authors, so there is no editio princeps in the usual sense: this anthology is the first printed collection of them (Commons calls it the 'first published anthology with presocratic texts'). The scan is a Google digitisation of a copy in the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale di Roma (ex-libris 'Ex Bibliotheca majori Coll. Rom. Societ. Jesu'). The page was identified from the Internet Archive's OCR text, not by looking at the image. The same book's title page is leaf 6 of this scan (archive.org/details/bub_gb_3J54VxKz_XUC/page/n6), and Commons has a separate photo of it from a Bloomsbury Auctions sale (File:Estienne_1573,_Poesis_philosophica.jpg, PD-US).
